  2. Implement 48‑hour on‑dock consolidation at hubs for eligible industrial shipments (hold low‑priority retail for 24–48h to combine loads and shift to full‑truck moves) with site SOPs and KPI (Impact: raises load factor 4–8%; Assumes customer SLAs permit short holds and warehouse space exists).

  5. Quick fuel & driver efficiency bundle: deploy a 30‑day driver eco‑driving blitz (coaching + leaderboard), check tire pressure & small maintenance sweep, and tighten fuel-card theft/exception monitoring (Impact: reduces fuel burn ~2–4% and lowers non‑fuel variances; Assumes driver cooperation and MAINT capacity). 
  6. Short data‑stabilization sprint: prioritize filling the “est.” KPI gaps by assigning a data owner to reconcile lane volumes, load factors and on‑time percent within 21 days to refine targets (Impact: enables accurate measurement and further gains; Assumes IT/ops can allocate 0.2–0.5 FTE temporarily).

1) Subtask restatement: convert the four prioritized linehaul quick‑wins into a sequenced 12‑month “who does what when” roadmap that hits ≥3% cost/mi reduction while staying under the $1.2M incremental spend cap and showing where spend (vs. process change) is expected. 

2) 12‑month roadmap (concrete steps): 1) Q1 (weeks 1–12) — Ops Lead & Dispatch: run a 6‑week backhaul‑pairing pilot using a 72‑hr rolling pairing rule, run a 21‑day data sprint (assign 0.2 FTE data owner) to replace “est.” KPIs, and deploy a 30‑day eco‑driving + maintenance blitz (process + small incentives); 2) Q2 — Regional Ops & Hubs: scale pairing and start 48‑hour on‑dock consolidation pilots at 2–3 high‑volume hubs (create SOPs, KPI dashboards) and Sales/Legal implement temporary corridor pricing guardrails for East‑Central & Central‑South; 3) Q3 — Fleet & Dispatch: full regional rollout of consolidation and dispatch rule updates plus asset right‑sizing (trailer retagging/refit phased by corridor); 4) Q4 — COO/Finance review: stabilise operations, run targeted driver incentives for retention, and decide on any analytics/telematics spend only if pilot ROI is validated. 

3) Expected impact, spend profile, key assumptions: projected contributions—backhaul pairing ~1.2%, consolidation ~1.0%, asset right‑sizing ~0.6%, pricing guardrails ~0.5%, eco‑driving ~0.2–0.4% (total ≈3.3–3.6% cost/mi); rough spend (process‑light near term) Q1 $30–80k (incentives, 0.2 FTE), Q2 $150–300k (dock tweaks, SOP rollout), Q3 $200–400k (trailer retagging/refit), Q4 $100–200k reserve for validated analytics/incentives — cumulative estimate $600–950k (keeps buffer vs. $1.2M); key assumptions: customers accept short 24–48h holds for consolidation, dispatch can reassign capacity quickly, and pilots deliver measurable empty‑mile reduction. 

4) Recommendation to drop/shrink lower‑priority items: defer any large telematics or full analytics platform purchases until Q4 post‑pilot (avoid front‑loading spend); keep a light analytics spend to support the data sprint but cap any single unapproved capital >$150k until pilots validate ROI. 

5) Implementation risks & mitigations: missing the 3% target if pilots underperform or customers resist (mitigate with conservative, measurable pilots, customer opt‑in/notice, and 30‑day pilot extensions), budget overrun from early capex (mitigate via monthly finance gates, require COO sign‑off for spends >$150k), and ops resistance (mitigate with regional pilot champions, short incentives, clear SOPs and weekly KPI reviews).
